name: Wall Push-Up
description: Stand about an arm's length from a wall. Place hands on the wall at chest height, a little wider than your shoulders. Bend your elbows to bring your chest toward the wall, then press back to straight arms.
cues: Body in one straight line, head to heels|Elbows angle back about 45°, not straight out to the sides|Chest comes close to the wall, then press all the way back
mistakes: Hips sagging or sticking out|Shrugging shoulders up to the ears|Tiny half reps
regression_tip: Stand a little closer to the wall.

name: High Incline Push-Up
equipment_notes: Kitchen counter or sturdy desk (~36 in / 90 cm)
description: Place hands on the edge of a sturdy counter, shoulder-width apart. Walk your feet back until your body is a straight, slanted line. Lower your chest to the edge, then press away.
cues: Squeeze glutes and brace your stomach like a plank|Lower your chest, not your chin, to the edge|Press until arms are straight
mistakes: Hips leading (piking) or sagging|Hands too far forward of shoulders|Bouncing off the edge
regression_tip: Step your feet closer to the counter.

name: Low Incline Push-Up
equipment_notes: Sturdy bench, low step, or 3rd-4th stair (~18 in / 45 cm)
description: Same as the high incline push-up, but with hands on a lower surface such as a bench or stair. The lower the surface, the harder it gets.
cues: Straight line from head to heels|Hands under or just outside the shoulders|Touch chest to the surface each rep
mistakes: Letting the lower back sag|Flaring elbows straight out|Looking up and craning the neck
regression_tip: Use a higher surface.
safety_note: Make sure the bench or step cannot slide or tip.

name: Knee Push-Up
equipment_notes: Floor; fold a towel under your knees
description: Kneel on the floor with hands under your shoulders. Walk your hands forward until there is a straight line from knees to head. Lower your chest to just above the floor, then press up.
cues: Hips stay in line with knees and shoulders|Chest to about a fist's height above the floor|Lock arms out fully at the top
mistakes: Hips piked up in the air|Head dipping toward the floor first|Hands placed too far forward
regression_tip: Go back to a low incline push-up for some sets.

name: Push-Up
description: Start in a high plank: hands under shoulders, legs straight, toes on the floor. Lower your whole body as one unit until your chest is a fist's height from the floor, then press up.
cues: Rigid plank: squeeze glutes and brace|Elbows about 45° from your body|Full range: chest low, arms straight at the top
mistakes: Sagging hips (the 'worm')|Only bending at the elbows a few inches|Holding your breath — exhale as you press
regression_tip: Do your first reps here, then finish the set on knees.

name: Decline Push-Up
equipment_notes: Feet on a stair, step or sofa (12-18 in / 30-45 cm)
description: A push-up with your feet raised on a low, stable surface. Raising the feet shifts more weight onto your arms and shoulders. This is a stretch goal past Week 12.
cues: Keep the plank rigid — no sagging|Hands slightly wider than shoulders|Lower under control, press strongly
mistakes: Feet too high too soon|Arching the lower back|Letting the head drop
regression_tip: Use a lower step, or return to regular push-ups.

name: Doorframe Row
description: Stand in an open doorway facing one side of the frame. Grip the frame edge with both hands at chest height, toes close to the frame. Lean back until your arms are straight, then pull your chest toward your hands.
cues: Lean back only as far as you can control|Squeeze shoulder blades together, then bend elbows|Keep your body straight like a plank
mistakes: Jerking or using your hips to pull|Shrugging shoulders up|Not straightening arms fully between reps
regression_tip: Stand more upright (step feet back from the frame).
safety_note: Grip firmly and keep feet close to the frame so you cannot slip far.

name: Bent-Knee Table Row
equipment_notes: Heavy, sturdy table (not folding or glass)
description: Lie on your back under a sturdy table, chest under the edge. Grip the edge with hands shoulder-width apart. Bend knees, feet flat. Lift hips so your body is straight from knees to shoulders and pull your chest to the table edge.
cues: Hips stay up in line with knees and shoulders|Pull elbows down and back toward your ribs|Lower slowly to straight arms
mistakes: Hips dropping toward the floor|Pulling with the neck/chin first|Short reps that stop halfway
regression_tip: Walk your feet closer to the table so you are less horizontal, or use the doorframe row.
safety_note: Test the table first: pull hard on the edge before getting under it. It must not tip or lift. If it moves, use the doorframe row instead.

name: Table Row
equipment_notes: Heavy, sturdy table (not folding or glass)
description: Same as the bent-knee table row, but with legs straight and heels on the floor. Your body forms one straight line from heels to head.
cues: Rigid body from heels to head|Chest touches (or nearly touches) the table edge|Control the lowering — 2 seconds down
mistakes: Hips sagging|Flaring elbows straight out|Reaching with the chin
regression_tip: Bend your knees (bent-knee table row).
safety_note: Test the table every time. Never use a folding or glass table.

name: Scapular Pull-Up
description: Hang from a pull-up bar with straight arms. Without bending your elbows, pull your shoulder blades down and back so your body rises an inch or two. Pause, then lower back to a full hang.
cues: Arms stay straight the whole time|Think 'shoulders away from ears'|Pause 1 second at the top
mistakes: Bending the elbows (turning it into a pull-up)|Swinging or kicking|Dropping fast out of the top
regression_tip: Keep your toes on a chair to take some weight.
safety_note: Check doorway bars are installed correctly and rated for your weight. Test before every session.

name: Feet-Elevated Table Row
equipment_notes: Sturdy table + chair or step for your heels
description: A table row with your heels resting on a chair or step about the same height as the table. Your body is close to horizontal, so you lift more of your weight. No bar needed.
cues: Body straight from heels to head|Pull chest all the way to the edge|Lower for 2 seconds
mistakes: Hips sagging between the supports|Heels slipping off the chair|Partial reps
regression_tip: Put your heels back on the floor (regular table row).
safety_note: Test the table and make sure the chair cannot slide.

name: Pull-Up Negative
equipment_notes: Pull-up bar + a sturdy step or chair
description: Use a step or chair to get your chin above the bar. Take your feet off and lower yourself slowly, taking 3-5 seconds, all the way to straight arms. Step back up and repeat. Keep sets to 5 reps or fewer.
cues: Start with chin over bar and elbows tight to your sides|Lower in 3-5 slow seconds, all the way down|Step back up — do not jump into the rep
mistakes: Dropping quickly through the bottom half|Kicking legs to slow down|Doing too many: negatives make you very sore at first
regression_tip: Do scapular pull-ups or a slower table row instead.
safety_note: Limit to 3-5 reps per set the first week you use them; they cause more soreness than usual.

name: Slow Feet-Elevated Table Row
description: A feet-elevated table row with a 3-second pause with your chest at the table, then a slow 4-second lowering. The slow tempo builds pull-up strength without a bar.
cues: Pause 3 seconds at the top, shoulder blades squeezed|Lower over 4 seconds|Keep the plank tight
mistakes: Rushing the lowering|Hips sagging during the pause|Shrugging
regression_tip: Use normal speed, or put heels on the floor.
safety_note: Test the table and make sure the chair cannot slide.

name: Pull-Up
description: Hang from the bar with hands just wider than shoulders, palms facing away. Pull your shoulder blades down, then pull until your chin is over the bar. Lower to straight arms with control. This is a stretch goal past Week 12 for most beginners.
cues: Start every rep from a full hang|Drive elbows down toward your back pockets|Lower with control — no dropping
mistakes: Kicking or swinging (kipping)|Half reps that never reach straight arms|Craning the chin to 'reach' the bar
regression_tip: Do 1-2 full reps, then finish the set with negatives.

name: Archer Table Row
description: A straight-leg table row with hands wide. Pull your chest toward one hand while the other arm stays nearly straight and only assists. Alternate sides. The hardest no-bar pulling level.
cues: The working arm does most of the pulling|Assisting arm stays nearly straight|Keep hips level — no twisting
mistakes: Rotating the body toward the working side|Bending the assisting arm a lot|Rushing
regression_tip: Go back to the slow feet-elevated table row.
safety_note: Test the table first; it must not tip.

name: Box Squat
equipment_notes: Sturdy chair or bench against a wall
description: Stand in front of a sturdy chair, feet shoulder-width apart. Sit back and down until you lightly touch the seat, then stand back up without rocking or using your hands.
cues: Sit back like you are reaching for the chair with your hips|Knees follow the direction of your toes|Light touch — don't plop down
mistakes: Knees caving inward|Rocking forward to get up|Heels lifting off the floor
regression_tip: Use a higher seat, or hold a counter lightly.
safety_note: Put the chair against a wall so it cannot slide.

name: Bodyweight Squat
description: Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart, toes turned slightly out. Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower as deep as you can with a flat back (aim for thighs parallel to the floor), then stand up tall.
cues: Weight across the whole foot, heels down|Knees track over toes|Chest proud, back flat
mistakes: Heels lifting|Knees collapsing inward|Rounding the lower back at the bottom
regression_tip: Squat to a chair (box squat).

name: Split Squat
equipment_notes: None (hold a wall for balance if needed)
description: Take a long step forward so your feet are hip-width apart, like standing on train tracks. Lower straight down until your back knee is just above the floor, then push back up. Do all reps on one side, then switch.
cues: Torso tall, move straight up and down|Front knee tracks over the middle toes|Back knee lightly approaches the floor
mistakes: Feet in a narrow 'tightrope' line (wobbly)|Front heel lifting|Pushing off the back foot instead of the front leg
regression_tip: Use a shorter range or hold a wall.

name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
equipment_notes: Chair, couch or step behind you
description: Stand about two feet in front of a chair. Place the top of one foot on the seat behind you. Lower until your front thigh is near parallel, then drive up through the front foot.
cues: Most weight on the front leg|Slight forward lean is fine; keep back flat|Control the bottom — no bouncing
mistakes: Standing too close to the chair|Front knee caving in|Rushing and losing balance
regression_tip: Use a lower step for the back foot, or regular split squats.
safety_note: Use a chair that cannot slide; hold a wall for balance if needed.

name: Box Pistol
equipment_notes: Sturdy chair or bench against a wall
description: Stand in front of a chair on one leg, the other leg held slightly forward. Slowly lower on one leg until you sit on the chair, then stand up on that same leg. Use a doorframe lightly for balance if needed.
cues: Lower slowly — at least 3 seconds|Working knee tracks over the toes|Stand up without swinging the free leg
mistakes: Dropping onto the seat|Knee collapsing inward|Pushing off with the free foot
regression_tip: Use a higher seat or hold a doorframe.
safety_note: Chair against a wall; keep a support within reach.

name: Assisted Pistol Squat
description: Hold a doorframe or pole. Stand on one leg with the other leg out in front. Lower all the way down on one leg, using your hands as little as possible, then stand back up. A stretch goal past Week 12.
cues: Arms only help — legs do the work|Heel stays flat|Keep the free leg off the floor
mistakes: Pulling with the arms|Collapsing at the bottom|Heel lifting
regression_tip: Do box pistols with a lower seat.

name: Glute Bridge
description: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart. Press through your heels to lift your hips until your body is straight from knees to shoulders. Squeeze your glutes for 1 second, then lower.
cues: Push through your heels|Squeeze glutes at the top — don't arch your back|Ribs down, stomach braced
mistakes: Over-arching the lower back|Feet too far from your hips|Rushing the top squeeze
regression_tip: Lift only partway, or bring feet a little closer.

name: Couch Hip Thrust
equipment_notes: Couch, sturdy bench or bed edge
description: Sit on the floor with your upper back against the edge of a couch, knees bent, feet flat. Drive your hips up until your body is level from knees to shoulders. Pause 1 second, then lower.
cues: Chin tucked, eyes forward|Shins vertical at the top|Squeeze glutes hard for 1 second
mistakes: Arching the lower back to get higher|Pushing through the toes|Couch sliding away
regression_tip: Go back to floor glute bridges.
safety_note: Push the couch or bench against a wall so it cannot slide.

name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
description: A glute bridge with one foot on the floor and the other knee pulled toward your chest or the leg held straight. Drive up through the planted heel. Do all reps on one side, then switch.
cues: Hips stay level — don't let one side drop|Drive through the heel|Pause at the top
mistakes: Twisting the pelvis|Arching the back|Pushing with the free leg
regression_tip: Keep both feet down but put more weight on one leg.

name: Single-Leg Hip Thrust
equipment_notes: Couch, sturdy bench or bed edge
description: A hip thrust with your upper back on the couch and only one foot on the floor. Drive your hips up until level, pause, and lower with control.
cues: Hips level side to side|Working shin vertical at the top|Controlled 2-second lowering
mistakes: Hips tilting|Over-arching the lower back|Bouncing off the floor
regression_tip: Do single-leg bridges on the floor.
safety_note: Bench or couch against a wall.

name: Dead Bug
description: Lie on your back, arms pointing at the ceiling, knees bent at 90° over your hips. Press your lower back gently into the floor. Slowly lower one arm overhead and the opposite leg toward the floor, then return and switch sides.
cues: Lower back stays pressed into the floor|Move slowly — 2-3 seconds each way|Breathe out as you reach
mistakes: Lower back arching off the floor|Moving fast|Holding your breath
regression_tip: Move only the legs (heel taps), keep arms still.

name: Forearm Plank
description: Rest on your forearms and toes, elbows under shoulders. Make a straight line from head to heels and hold, breathing normally.
cues: Squeeze glutes and brace your stomach|Push the floor away with your forearms|Neutral neck — look at the floor
mistakes: Hips sagging|Hips piked high|Holding your breath
regression_tip: Drop to your knees, or place forearms on a bench.

name: Tuck Hollow Hold
description: Lie on your back. Press your lower back into the floor, lift your head and shoulders, and pull your knees in over your hips. Reach your hands toward your knees and hold.
cues: Lower back glued to the floor|Shoulder blades just off the floor|Breathe slowly through the hold
mistakes: Lower back lifting|Straining the neck — chin slightly tucked|Holding your breath
regression_tip: Keep your head down, or do dead bugs.

name: Hollow Body Hold
description: From the tuck hollow position, extend your legs out straight and low, and reach your arms overhead, keeping your lower back pressed into the floor. Your body forms a shallow banana shape.
cues: Lower back stays down — raise legs higher if it lifts|Arms by ears, legs together|Point toes, squeeze legs
mistakes: Lower back arching off the floor|Legs too low too soon|Neck strain
regression_tip: Bend knees slightly or bring arms forward.

name: Knee Side Plank
description: Lie on your side, propped on your forearm with the elbow under the shoulder and knees bent behind you. Lift your hips so your body is straight from knees to head and hold. Switch sides.
cues: Elbow directly under shoulder|Hips pushed forward, not back|Top hand on hip, chest open
mistakes: Hips sagging toward the floor|Rolling forward or backward|Shrugging into the shoulder
regression_tip: Hold for shorter sets with brief rests.

name: Side Plank
description: A side plank with legs straight and feet stacked (or staggered for balance). Lift your hips into a straight line and hold. Switch sides.
cues: Straight line from head to feet|Push the floor away with your forearm|Squeeze glutes
mistakes: Hips dropping|Piking at the hips|Neck tilting down
regression_tip: Stagger your feet, or go back to the knee side plank.

name: Side Plank with Leg Lift
description: From a full side plank, lift your top leg a few inches and hold it up for the whole set. Switch sides.
cues: Bottom hip stays high|Top leg straight, lifted about 6 in / 15 cm|Steady breathing
mistakes: Hips dropping as the leg lifts|Rotating the chest toward the floor|Bending the top knee
regression_tip: Lower the top leg for part of the hold.

name: March or Jog in Place
description: Easy marching or a light jog to raise your heart rate.
cues: Stay light on your feet|Swing your arms

name: Arm Circles
description: Arms out to the sides; make small circles that grow bigger, forward then backward.
cues: Start small, finish big|Relax your neck

name: Cat-Cow
description: On hands and knees, slowly round your back up (cat), then let it dip as you look forward (cow).
cues: Move one segment at a time|Breathe with the movement

name: Hip Hinge Drill
description: Hands on hips, knees soft. Push your hips back with a flat back until you feel your hamstrings, then stand tall and squeeze your glutes.
cues: Hips go back, not down|Back stays flat

name: Wall Slide
description: Back against a wall, arms in a 'goal post' shape. Slide arms up the wall and back down without arching your back.
cues: Ribs down|Only go as high as you can control

name: Reverse Lunge with Reach
description: Step back into a gentle lunge and reach both arms overhead. Step back up and switch.
cues: Small, comfortable range|Tall torso

name: Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
description: Kneel on one knee, other foot in front. Squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg and shift forward gently until you feel a stretch at the front of the hip.
cues: Mild stretch, never pain|Breathe slowly

name: Doorway Chest Stretch
description: Forearm on a doorframe at shoulder height. Step through gently until you feel a stretch across the chest.
cues: Mild stretch, never pain|Breathe slowly

name: Lying Hamstring Stretch
description: Lie on your back; loop a towel around one foot and raise the straight leg until you feel a mild stretch behind the thigh.
cues: Mild stretch, never pain|Breathe slowly

name: Figure-4 Glute Stretch
description: Lie on your back, cross one ankle over the opposite knee, and pull the bottom leg toward you.
cues: Mild stretch, never pain|Breathe slowly

name: Child's Pose
description: Kneel, sit hips back toward heels, and reach your arms forward on the floor. Breathe into your back.
cues: Mild stretch, never pain|Breathe slowly

name: Box Breathing
description: Breathe in 4 seconds, hold 4, out 4, hold 4. Let your heart rate settle.
cues: Mild stretch, never pain|Breathe slowly
